notes.title: Potential Agents to Add:
body: Pre-visit briefing agent. Each morning, it builds a short card for each stop on today's leg: past notes, who to ask for, which pitch to lead with, and what's on the dealer's lot from their own website. It saves reps from scrolling notes in the parking lot.

Weekly digest agent. It reads the sync log and emails Ken or the team lead a summary of stops visited per rep, hot leads, dealers that went quiet, and anything flagged for a return visit. It's cheap to build because the data already exists.

Copart Dealer Services handoff agent. When a visit is marked as interested, it drafts the handoff to the Copart Dealer Services rep with everything gathered so far. It can also draft a follow-up text for the field rep to send.
For scaling to new yards

Route builder agent. You give it a yard address and it researches about 30 dealers, checks each address and phone against real sources, groups them into legs, and outputs the dealer list with confidence flags and caveats. notes.title: Lead Tracker design
body: The Lead Tracker is the lead list for the whole Copart Dealer Services sales team, office and field. Built on Work Claude from the US dealer map. It is the CRM (d-udm-01).

Who owns what: the Lead Tracker owns who the dealer is (identity, sources, Copart status, score, owner, stage, every touch). The Route Tracker is the field screen. It pulls each rep's assigned leads and sends visit events back by lead ID. Events are added, never overwritten.

Lead record: lead ID; name, address, pin, phone, email, website, each with a source, date collected and verified flag; play, score, one-line reason, Copart status (active, inactive, none); team, owner, channel, claimed date, return date; stage, last touch, next action and date, outcome reason; event log.

Stages: New, Qualified, Assigned, Contacted, Meeting set, Visited, Seller form sent, Account open, First car, Active seller. Off-ramps: Not a fit, Closed business, Snoozed, Returned to pool. Meeting set is the meetings-booked number and the point where office hands to field.

Two roles: office sales works by phone and email (inbound leads, the long tail across 28 states, qualifying, booking visits, onboarding). Field reps work by visit (dense territories, key accounts, visits the office booked).

Each lead gets a channel: office first (the default), field direct (dealer groups, tier A near a yard, dealers already on a route) or office only (outside any field territory). One owner at a time; ownership changes only through a handoff.
Lead sources: state license pulls and new licenses, Marketing's dealer list, website form leads, the hotline, Ken's new-license leads, and dealers reps add from the road. Every lead keeps its source.
Active Copart sellers come off prospect lists, inactive dealers go to win-back, no status are prospects (udm-01).

Build order: lead record and stages, a lead page per team (udm-04), the Route Tracker connection (udm-05), then the CRM screens (udm-06). The agents that fill and work the list are in the Agentic Workflow project.

notes.title: Sales workflow, from the whiteboard
body: Chase's board (Oct 16) is how every project is placed from now on. Full write-up in docs/sales-workflow.md.

Prospective and inactive approach, three branches: get found (AEO and SEO, webpage changes), go get 'em (digital campaigns: new vs inactive, direct vs indirect, email, call, text, paid ads; marketing tools and apps), convert 'em (web forms, the prospective and inactive dealer outreach campaigns).

Lead Tracker with CRM at the center: supplies dealer profiles by state and status, assigns leads to teams, is the audience for campaigns, and logs recommended touch dates and tracked responses back to the dealer profile.

Agents: A1 Dealer profile (pulls info from the dealer site), A2 AEO and dealer listening, A3 pre-call and follow-up drafter, A4 dormant dealer activation. All loop with each other and feed one agent pipeline. Break the dealer map into segments: leads by team.
Leads by team: field reps by ZIP code and city with in-person visits on the Route Tracker; office (inside) sales works all leads with follow-up.

Route Tracker: pre-visit (route building, dealer profile, outreach with the exclusive offer email template, team roster), dealer visit (contact, profile fields, assignments), follow-up (handoff, hot, mild or cold, send to team), then CRM for Route Tracker leads. The Route Tracker and the Lead Tracker talk to each other.

Separate from that approach, the Copilot and Power Automate tools: Copart Dealer Services AI (Teams agent: pre-call brief, updates, follow-up; ideas: track the full process, manager view) and meeting management (memory bank with call transcripts and a SharePoint meetings site; chief of staff agent with Teams messages, automated updates and the weekly session; PLAUD email to an Outlook PLAUD folder; one automated workflow connecting everything). Built so far: meeting transcript reader, auto draft email, auto schedule meeting, PLAUD autoflow to email.
Left off the tracker on purpose: the promotion leads list, the DJ and Ben team lists, the slump list and the top sellers questions.
